title: Mouse tail skin wholemount staining and intravital calcium imaging
protocol: Use postnatal day 18 mice for the experiment.
Sacrifice mice using CO2.
Mark the middle one third of the dorsal tail along the anterior-posterior central axis.
Mark the ventral midline of the mouse tail.
Cut along the marked ventral midline with a pair of surgical scissors.
Remove the skin from the tail bone using surgical tweezers.
Cut the middle one third of the dorsal side tail skin into pieces, each measuring 0.5 cm by 0.5 cm.
Place the cut skin pieces in at least 5 mL of 25 mM EDTA in 1× PBS buffer.
Incubate on an orbital shaker at 37°C and 150 rpm for 2 hours.
Separate the epidermis with attached hair follicles from the dermis using fine-tipped tweezers, moving from anterior to posterior.
Place removed epidermis with attached hair follicles in 1 mL of 4% formaldehyde in 1× PBS buffer.
Incubate at room temperature for 7 minutes.
Remove the epidermis and wash with 1 mL of 1× PBS for 3 × 30 min on an orbital shaker at 80 rpm at room temperature.
Incubate tissues in 1 mL 0.3% TritonX-100 in 1× PBS for 10–20 min.
Wash samples with 1 mL 1× PBS for 3 × 20 min at room temperature.
Incubate the epidermis with attached hair follicles in 1 mL blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate the epidermis with attached hair follicles with primary antibody (diluted in blocking solution) overnight (∼16 h) at 4°C.
Incubate samples with secondary antibody and 1 μg/mL DAPI diluted in blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash samples with 1× PBS for 3 × 20 min at room temperature.
Remove unwanted hair follicles using fine-tipped tweezers under a stereo microscope if needed.
Place the tissue on the slide with the side of the hair follicle facing the coverslip.
Mount the tissue with 50% glycerol diluted in PBS containing 1 μg/mL DAPI.
Apply coverslip to the epidermis wholemount tissue.
Seal edges of the coverslip with clear nail polish.
Add 50 μl mounting buffer for each 0.5 cm × 0.5 cm epidermis wholemount tissue.
Prepare tamoxifen solution at 10 mg/mL in 100% sunflower oil.
Heat the tamoxifen solution to 37°C and vortex at 200 rpm for 30 min to dissolve tamoxifen.
Inject Sox9creERT2; GCaMP6s; Ai14 mice intraperitoneally with tamoxifen at a dosage of 40 μg/g body weight on postnatal day 11, repeated for 3 consecutive days.
Anesthetize mouse using isoflurane.
Prepare the imaging station by immobilizing a 15 × 25 cm heating plate of the Temperature Controller on the microscopic table.
Set the temperature of the heating plate at 37°C for the duration of the imaging process.
Immobilize the breathing apparatus of an Anesthesia System by tapes on one side of the heating plate.
Put the anesthetized mouse nostril inside the breathing apparatus of the Anesthesia System.
Immobilize the mouse tail by taping it to the heating plate.
Stabilize the tail skin around the imaging area using extra tapes.
Adjust the microscopic lens to be positioned just above the intended imaging skin area.
Perform Ca2+ imaging using a Nikon 2-photon microscope with a 25× water-immersion objective lens with a numerical aperture of 1.02.
Tune the laser to the 910 nm wavelength with 40% intensity for imaging GCaMP6s signals.
Tune the laser to the 1,040 nm wavelength with 10% intensity for imaging tdTomato signals.
Acquire images at 1 frame per 10 seconds for 10 minutes using Nikon software.
